title: Fermi sech modulus: |Gamma(1/2 + i y)|^2 = pi / cosh(pi y)
latent_structure: The Fermi (sech) thermal kernel is the modulus squared of Gamma on the critical line Re z=1/2. Compact hyperbolic object sech(pi y) vs a product of Gamma values. This is the real-modulus identity (A&S 6.1.30 / DLMF 5.4.4), not the Im-digamma pair 5.4.16--5.4.17 (tanh/coth of psi). Logarithmic derivative of this identity is Re psi, a different residual.

function_domains.gamma: Gamma meromorphic; simple poles at z=0,-1,-2,... (DLMF 5.2.1); no zeros
function_domains.cosh: entire; zeros at I*(n+1/2)*pi, none on the real axis

nonzero_conditions.label: DERIVED
nonzero_conditions.source: zeros of cosh are at I*(n+1/2)*pi; pi y is real for real y, so cosh(pi y)>=1

analytic_domains.statement: 1/2 + I y is not a nonpositive integer (so Gamma(1/2+I y) is defined)
analytic_domains.label: DERIVED
analytic_domains.source: DLMF 5.2.1 poles at 0,-1,-2,...; Re(1/2+I y)=1/2 for real y

analytic_domains.statement: 1/2 - I y is not a nonpositive integer
analytic_domains.label: DERIVED

branch_conventions: DLMF writes Gamma(1/2+i y) Gamma(1/2-i y) = |Gamma(1/2+i y)|^2; modulus of a nonzero meromorphic value, no extra branch

derived_conditions.statement: both Gamma factors are finite and nonzero for all real y
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Gamma has no zeros; poles excluded by Re=1/2

why_not_cse_lgg: A product of two Gamma values vs a single hyperbolic function. CSE cannot invent sech (or 1/cosh) as the compact Fermi modulus kernel. LGG does not introduce Gamma on 1/2+i R.
proposer_leak_risk: Source names Gamma, cosh, and the line 1/2+i y. Do not leak 'Fermi-Dirac', 'sech occupation', 'Im digamma', or 'thermal-01 partner' as gold names. Residual is the product-minus-pi/cosh only.
notes: SymPy-writable: gamma, cosh, pi, I. Distinct from thermal-01 (Im psi(1/2+iy)=(pi/2) tanh) and thermal-02 (Im psi(iy)=coth). y=0 is allowed: Gamma(1/2)^2=pi=pi/cosh(0). No T>0 import.
